physicalNotes: Radius 0.18734945 Jupiter radii from Díez Alonso et al. 2019 (2019MNRAS.489.5928D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.489.5928D/abstract): 13,394 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0159 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Díez Alonso et al. 2019 (2019MNRAS.489.5928D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname D_IACUTE_EZ_ALONSO_ET_AL__2019): P 27.359 d
sources.shape: Díez Alonso et al. 2019 (2019MNRAS.489.5928D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname D_IACUTE_EZ_ALONSO_ET_AL__2019): a/R* 63; Díez Alonso et al. 2019 (2019MNRAS.489.5928D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname D_IACUTE_EZ_ALONSO_ET_AL__2019): inclination 89.67 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Díez Alonso et al. 2019 (2019MNRAS.489.5928D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname D_IACUTE_EZ_ALONSO_ET_AL__2019): transit mid-time 2458010.417 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 799 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
